fields.bio:
Forever game master since 2014, player whenever someone else is brave enough to run. I like slow-burn mysteries, talkative villains and maps drawn on graph paper.

Free on Thursday evenings and most Saturdays. Happy to help new players build a first character.

Game master for beginners and for anyone who thinks they are 'not a roleplayer'. I run the Thursday game on the Dragon Coast and the beginner's table at the club.

Plays druids. Always druids.
Loud dice, louder dwarves. I run heists and one-shots, and play whoever stands in the front line.
Horror and folk tales. I run Lanterns Over Blackmoor on Sundays and play far too many rangers.
Artificers and other people who fix things. Moved cities in May, so I mostly play online now.
Skyships, tea and monks. Game master of Skyship Smugglers. I keep session notes so the rest of the party does not have to.

Healer main, spreadsheet enthusiast. If your party has a loot ledger, I probably wrote it.

Planning my first campaign as a game master - wish me luck.

Seraphine sang at the Ember Court for six years and listened for seven. When her mentor, Maestro Oriel Vance, vanished between two verses of a duet, the court called it a scandal and moved on. She did not.

She left with his lute, a list of names and a talent for being invited to places she should not be.

fields.title: Tomb of the Clockwork King
fields.description:
A five-session dungeon crawl for a small party. Somewhere under the old observatory, a king who replaced his heart with a mainspring is still counting the seconds.

Classic exploration: traps, riddles, limited torches and one very patient boss. We finished in May - the notes stay here as a keepsake.

fields.title: Curse of the Emerald Crown
fields.description:
A gothic mystery for heroes of levels 3-8. The town of Greywater has been without a ruler for thirty years, and the crown that was broken to end the last one is trying to put itself back together.

Expect investigation, uneasy alliances and choices that come back later. We play every second Saturday evening, mostly online, with an in-person game once a season.

New players are welcome: join, choose a character of level 5 and say hello in the notes.

fields.title: Ashes of the Dragon Coast
fields.description:
Pirates, volcanoes and a dragon who collects debts instead of gold. A swashbuckling sandbox on a chain of smoking islands.

Thursday evenings online. Sessions are short, about two and a half hours, so please answer each session in advance: we play with three players or more.

fields.title: Skyship Smugglers
fields.description:
The crew of the Marigold moves cargo that the Sky Guild would rather not know about. Episodic jobs, a shared ship sheet and a running tab in every port.

Friday nights online. There is one free bunk on the ship: join as a player and bring a hero of level 6.

fields.title: Lanterns Over Blackmoor
fields.description:
Folk horror in a fog-bound village where the lanterns must never go out. Low magic, high tension, and a map that changes when nobody is looking.

Sundays at the club. Bring a character of level 3.

fields.title: The Harvest Moon Heist
fields.description: A one-shot in two parts: one night, one vault and one harvest festival to hide in. Careful plans, improvised disasters.

fields.title: The Sunken Library of Aram
fields.description:
An expedition into a flooded archive where every book remembers its last reader. I am still gathering the party: three or four players who enjoy puzzles and slow exploration.

We start with a session zero in November.

fields.title: Beginner's Table: Goblin Trouble
fields.description: Never played before? This table is for you. A short, friendly adventure that teaches the rules as we go: no preparation is needed, dice and ready-made heroes are provided.

fields.title: Session 1: The Brass Door
fields.agenda:
Meet at the ruins of the old observatory.
The riddle of the brass door.
First level: the winding galleries.
fields.summary:
The party talked their way past the caretaker automaton by posing as royal clock inspectors. Hester found the hidden key inside the sundial; Fenwick set off exactly one trap, loudly.

We stopped at the top of the great stair with two torches left.

fields.title: Session 2: Gears and Ghosts
fields.agenda:
The great stair and the gallery of stopped clocks.
First meeting with the ghost of the royal clockmaker.
A chance to rest - if they find the winding room.
fields.summary:
Sam could not make it, so Fenwick spent the session 'guarding the rear'. The clockmaker's ghost offered a deal: wind every clock in the gallery and she opens the lower door.

Sable wound the wrong clock first. A fight with four brass hounds; everybody is alive, nobody is happy.

fields.title: Session 0: Characters and expectations
fields.agenda:
Tone, safety tools and house rules.
Build the party together: why do you travel as a group?
A short prologue on the road.
fields.summary: Five heroes, one shared secret: each of them received the same unsigned letter. We agreed on a gothic tone with room for jokes, and on every second Saturday.

fields.title: Session 3: The Winding Stair
fields.agenda:
Descent to the second level.
The pendulum bridge.

fields.title: Session 1: The Road to Greywater
fields.agenda:
Ambush at the toll bridge.
Arrival in Greywater.
The ferryman's warning.
fields.summary:
The 'guards' of the toll bridge turned out to be starving farmers; Thessaly talked them down and Durgan paid the toll anyway. In Greywater nobody says the word 'crown' out loud.

Old Tobias ferried the party across for free and told them not to stay after dark.

fields.title: Session 3: The Winding Stair (take two)
fields.agenda:
Descent to the second level.
The pendulum bridge.
The vault of spare hearts.
fields.summary:
The pendulum bridge took most of the evening and one of Hester's crossbows. In the vault the party found seven brass hearts and one empty stand.

Cliffhanger: something downstairs started ticking faster.

fields.title: Finale: The Clockwork King
fields.agenda:
The throne room.
The king's offer.
Epilogues for every hero.
fields.summary:
Played online because of the long weekend. The king offered each hero more time - literally. Sable said yes, then changed her mind at the worst possible moment.

Fenwick's last song stopped the mainspring for one round, and Hester did not miss. The tomb is silent now. The epilogues are in the campaign notes.

fields.title: Session 2: The Drowned Chapel
fields.agenda:
Explore the flooded chapel.
The first shard.
fields.summary:
Kiri crossed the nave without touching the water. Everybody else touched the water. The first shard of the crown was inside the font, guarded by something that used to be the priest.

Maelis laid it to rest. The party has the shard, and the shard knows it.

fields.title: Session 3: A Bargain at the Hanging Tree
fields.agenda:
The night market under the hanging tree.
Who else is looking for the shards?
fields.summary:
Fenwick traded a true story for a false map and considers it a fair deal. Durgan's creditors caught up with him - see his quest note.

A masked woman bought the party a drink and knew all their names.

fields.title: Session 1: Smoke on the Water
fields.agenda:
Arrival at Cinder Bay.
A job offer from the harbour master.
fields.summary: The ship that brought the heroes burned at anchor on the first night - not their fault, for once. Seraphine recognised the arsonist's song. Nim acquired a harbour pass that is almost genuine.

fields.title: Session 4: Masquerade at Castle Verrin
fields.agenda:
An in-person game at the club - bring a mask if you have one.
The regent's masquerade.
Steal the second shard, or win it.
fields.summary:
Our first game around a real table. Lady Verrin danced with every hero in turn and learned something from each of them.

The second shard is in the party's hands, the regent's mask is cracked, and Greywater now has a reason to remember their faces.

fields.title: Session 2: The Salt Market
fields.agenda:
Follow the song.
The auction of impounded cargo.
fields.summary:
A bidding war against a masked agent of the Red Admiral. The party won a crate they could not afford and paid with a promise.

Inside the crate: a sleeping dragon wyrmling.

fields.title: Session 3: Wyrmling's Hoard
fields.agenda:
What do you feed a wyrmling?
The smugglers' caves.
fields.summary: Played without Seraphine, who was 'gathering information' in town. Quill taught the wyrmling to fetch. The caves hold the first real clue about the missing mentor.

fields.title: Job 1: The Cloudport Run
fields.agenda:
Meet the crew of the Marigold.
A simple delivery.
fields.summary: It was not a simple delivery. Wren kept the engine alive with a wrench and a lullaby; Hester came aboard as the bounty hunter sent to catch the crew and left as a member of it.

fields.title: Session 4: Fire Season
fields.agenda:
The volcano wakes.
Evacuate the lower town or chase the arsonist.
fields.summary:
The party split up and it almost worked. Seraphine caught the arsonist on the rooftops; Nim and Quill got forty people onto boats.

The arsonist was paid in the Red Admiral's coin.

fields.title: Session 5: Into the Thornwood
fields.agenda:
Back from the summer break: a short recap first.
The path that moves.
The hermit of the Thornwood.
fields.summary:
The forest does not like metal, and it told Durgan so. Thessaly negotiated safe passage in exchange for a promise she has not explained to the others yet.

The third shard is not in the Thornwood. It was moved - recently.

fields.title: Job 2: Customs, Bribes and Other Inconveniences of Honest Smuggling
fields.agenda:
Inspection at the Skygate.
Hide the cargo. Hide the other cargo.
fields.summary: The inspector found nothing, mostly because the cargo had hatched and left on its own. The crew is two crates short and one very loyal cloud-ray richer.

fields.title: Session 1: The Fog Comes In
fields.agenda:
Arrive in Blackmoor before dusk.
Meet the lamplighter.
fields.summary: The road ended at a village that is not on any map. Ember lit a lantern with her own fire and the whole square went quiet. Captain Marr counted the lanterns twice and got two different numbers.

fields.title: Session 5: The Ember Court
fields.agenda:
An invitation that cannot be refused.
Old Barnaby joins the party.
fields.summary: Welcome, Oleh! Barnaby arrived as a badger and stayed that way for most of the audience. The dragon of the Ember Court does not want gold - she wants debts, and now the party owes her one.

fields.title: Session 6: The Emerald Vault
fields.agenda:
Under Castle Verrin.
Three locks, three keepers.
fields.summary:
A proper dungeon night. Two of the three keepers were bargained with; the third had to be fought on a staircase that kept rearranging itself.

Inside the vault: an empty cushion and a fresh set of footprints leading out.

fields.title: Job 3: Storm Front
fields.agenda: Outrun the storm or fly through it.
fields.summary: They flew through it. The Marigold needs a new mast, and the Sky Guild now has a very good description of the ship.

fields.title: Part one: Casing the vault
fields.agenda:
Pick the roles: face, muscle, eyes.
The festival grounds.
Plan the job.
fields.summary: Three hours of planning, twenty minutes of action. Brakka got hired as a guard of the very vault the crew is robbing. Captain Marr charmed the blueprints out of the architect.

fields.title: Session 2: The Lamplighter's Debt
fields.agenda:
One lantern went out last night.
Ask around - carefully.
fields.summary: Three villagers, three versions of the same night. The lamplighter owes something to the bog, and the payment is due at the next new moon.

fields.title: Session 7: What the Crown Remembers
fields.agenda:
The vision in the vault.
The herald of the Hollow King.

fields.title: Part two: The getaway
fields.agenda: Midnight. The vault. Everything that can go wrong.
fields.summary:
Oleh could not come, so Varric 'ran the distraction' off-screen. The vault was already empty - somebody got there first. Brakka carried the whole door out as a consolation prize.

A perfect ending for a one-shot: no gold, one door and a harvest festival that nobody will forget.

fields.title: Session 6: Ash and Tide
fields.agenda:
Sail for the outer islands.
A storm, a wreck and a rescue.
fields.summary: The crossing went wrong in the best way. The party pulled six sailors out of the water, and one of them wears the ring of Seraphine's mentor.

fields.title: Session 3: Bog Lights
fields.agenda:
Online this week: the club is closed for a tournament.
Follow the lights into the bog.
fields.summary: A short session with one player. Ember followed the lights alone, which was exactly what they wanted. She came back with wet boots and a bell clapper that should not exist.

fields.title: Session 8: The Siege of Greywater
fields.agenda:
Maelis starts at 0 hit points: the round goes on from where we stopped.
The herald's ultimatum.
Defend the ferry or the castle - the party cannot hold both.

fields.title: Session 7: The Lighthouse Burns
fields.agenda:
The sailor's story.
The lighthouse on Gull Rock.

fields.title: Job 4: The Glass Archipelago
fields.agenda:
A buyer for the cloud-ray.
Nobody mentions the Guild.

fields.title: First game: learn by playing
fields.agenda:
No preparation is needed.
How a turn works.
A goblin problem at the mill.

fields.title: Session 4: The Drowned Bell
fields.agenda:
A third hero arrives in Blackmoor - welcome, Alex!
The bell under the water.

fields.title: Session 9: Beneath the Old Keep
fields.agenda: Depends on how the siege ends. Either way: the tunnels.

fields.title: Session 8: Parley with the Red Admiral
fields.agenda: A meeting under a white flag. Think about what your character wants from the Admiral.

fields.title: Session 5: Hollow Night
fields.agenda: New moon. The debt is due.

fields.title: Session zero: characters and house rules
fields.agenda:
Tone and expectations.
Build the characters together: level 1, any class.
Pick a regular day.

fields.title: Season finale: The Crown Breaks
fields.play_location: Dice & Dragons club, the big table
fields.agenda:
In person and long: we start two hours early and order pizza.
No spoilers here.

fields.title: Winter special: The Frozen Wake
fields.agenda: A standalone holiday adventure. Details later.

fields.title: Season two: A Town Without a Crown
Spring arc: Storm over Cinder Bay
The Clockwork King
fields.content:
He replaced his heart with a mainspring so that he would never run out of time. He has been winding down for two hundred years.

Not cruel, only afraid. He offers every visitor the same bargain: a little of their time for a little of his treasure.

fields.title: Campaign pitch and tone
fields.content:
Greywater is a town that agreed to forget. Thirty years ago its last ruler was overthrown and the Emerald Crown was broken into three shards, so that nobody could wear it again.

Tone: a gothic mystery with warm characters. Horror stays off-screen more often than not. Jokes at the table are welcome; jokes that break another player's scene are not.

What I expect: a hero who has a reason to stay in Greywater and a reason to trust at least one other hero.

fields.title: House rules
fields.content:
1. Flanking gives +2 to hit, not advantage.
2. A potion of healing is a bonus action for yourself and an action for somebody else.
3. Players give inspiration to each other, once per session.
4. If you miss a session, your hero is 'busy in town' and gains the same experience.
5. Critical hits: maximum damage on the first set of dice, then roll the second.

fields.title: Old Tobias, the ferryman
fields.content:
Ferried us across for free in session 1 and told us not to stay after dark. Knows more than he says.

Thessaly's impression: the river likes him. That counts for something.

To ask next time: who paid him to wait for us at the crossing?

fields.title: The tomb, level by level
fields.content:
Level 1 - the winding galleries: caretaker automata, the brass door, the sundial key.
Level 2 - the gallery of stopped clocks and the pendulum bridge.
Level 3 - the vault of spare hearts.
Level 4 - the throne room.

Every level is one hour 'later' than the one above it. Torches burn accordingly.

fields.title: Greywater
fields.content:
A river town of about two thousand people, built on both banks and on the pilings between them.

The Ferry Quarter - cheap rooms, loud taverns, Tobias's landing.
Chapel Hill - the drowned chapel sits at its foot.
Castle Verrin - closed to visitors except on festival nights.
The Hanging Tree - a night market grows around it every new moon.

Nobody in Greywater says the word 'crown'. They say 'the old hat'.

fields.title: Rumours from the Ferry Quarter
fields.content:
Collected by Wren before she left town:

The regent has not aged in thirty years.
The chapel flooded on the night the crown broke.
There were four shards, not three.

Good luck, everyone - I will miss this table!

fields.title: Epilogues: where the heroes ended up
fields.content:
Hester Crowfoot collected the bounty on the Clockwork King and took another contract the same evening. She was last seen boarding a skyship.

Fenwick Lark turned the whole thing into a ballad. In his version there were three kings.

Sable kept one brass heart. She says it is a souvenir. It ticks.

fields.title: The Emerald Crown (broken)
fields.content:
Wondrous item, legendary, in three pieces.

Each shard hums when another shard is within a mile. A hero who sleeps next to a shard dreams of a throne room they have never seen.

One shard: advantage on Insight checks against the people of Greywater.
Two shards: the bearer may ask the crown one question per week. It answers truthfully and unkindly.
Three shards: unknown.

fields.title: Durgan's debt to the Ironvein clan
fields.content:
Durgan owes the clan 300 gold pieces and one formal apology. The collectors found him at the Hanging Tree.

Paid so far: 120 gp.
Deadline: the first snow.

If anyone finds dwarven masonry work in Greywater, I am interested.

fields.title: Welcome to the Dragon Coast
fields.content:
Short sessions, big swings. The Dragon Coast rewards bold plans and punishes long debates.

Please answer every session at least two days ahead. With fewer than three confirmed players I move the game.

Heroes level up at milestones - roughly every three sessions.

fields.title: Cinder Bay
fields.content:
The only deep harbour on the coast, built inside a drowned crater.

Upper town: merchants, the harbour master, clean streets.
Lower town: everything else. Half of it was evacuated in session 4.
The Salt Market: opens at low tide, closes when the water reaches the stalls.

fields.title: Lady Verrin, the Masked Regent
fields.content:
Regent of Greywater in everything but name. Never seen without a porcelain mask; since the masquerade the mask has a crack across the left cheek.

Wants: the crown kept broken. Fears: what the heroes will do with two shards in one bag.

She is polite, patient and has not lied to the party yet - which worries them more than a lie would.

fields.title: Sea shanty playlist
fields.content:
Background music for the table: https://music.example.com/playlists/dragon-coast

Tracks 1-8 for sailing, 9-14 for taverns, 15 onwards for when the volcano does something.

fields.title: Crew charter of the Marigold
fields.content:
Equal shares. The ship gets a share too.
No job that puts passengers in danger.
Whoever breaks it, fixes it. Whoever cannot fix it, tells Wren.

Signed by the whole crew in session 1.

fields.title: Skyship rules cheat sheet
fields.content:
Ship actions on your turn: steer, repair, brace, lookout.
A repair check takes an action and tinker's tools.
Falling off the ship is survivable exactly once per character.

Full rules: https://files.example.com/marigold/skyship-rules.pdf

fields.title: The Red Admiral
fields.content:
Commands the largest free fleet on the coast. Nobody the party has met can describe her face.

Pays in red-gold coins stamped with a burning ship. The arsonist from session 4 carried a purse of them.

fields.title: Blackmoor village
fields.content:
Forty houses, one square, one chapel without a bell. A ring of lanterns marks the edge of the village; beyond it is the bog.

Rules that everybody here knows:
The lanterns are lit before dusk.
Nobody counts them out loud.
If a light moves, it is not a lantern.

fields.title: The Thornwood
fields.content:
What we learned in session 5:

The paths move, but only when nobody is looking at them. Kiri walked backwards for an hour and it worked.
The forest dislikes metal. Leave the armor in the cart.
The hermit trades in promises. Thessaly made one. We still do not know what it was.

fields.title: Marks and guards
fields.content:
Reeve Aldermoss - keeps the vault key on a chain, loves pie.
Sergeant Pell - honest, tired, two days from retirement.
The architect - proud of the vault and happy to explain why it cannot be robbed.

fields.title: Things we should not have stolen
fields.content:
A harbour pass that is almost genuine.
One dragon wyrmling (technically bought, not stolen).
The harbour master's second-best hat.
A red-gold coin that feels warm on the night before something burns.

Nim would like the record to show that the hat was a gift.

fields.title: Maps and handouts
fields.content:
Town map of Greywater: https://files.example.com/emerald-crown/greywater-map.png
The unsigned letter (handout from session 0): https://files.example.com/emerald-crown/letter.pdf
Family tree of the Verrin line: https://files.example.com/emerald-crown/verrin-tree.pdf

I update the town map after every session. The fog of war is on purpose.

fields.title: The three shards of the crown
fields.content:
First shard - found in the drowned chapel (session 2). Carried by Maelis.
Second shard - won at the masquerade (session 4). Carried by Fenwick, allegedly.
Third shard - lay in the Emerald Vault until very recently. Somebody took it before the party arrived.

Open question: the shards pull towards each other. What happens when all three are in one room?

fields.title: Cargo manifest
fields.content:
Official: 40 crates of dried plums.
Actual: 38 crates of dried plums, 1 crate of unstamped sky-silk, 1 empty crate with claw marks.

Also on board: a cloud-ray that thinks Wren is its mother.

fields.title: What I am planning
fields.content:
A slow exploration game: one flooded floor of the library per session, with puzzles that reward notes and patience.

Characters start at level 1. Scholars, divers and treasure hunters all fit.

If the idea sounds good, join the campaign and answer the session zero.

fields.title: Who is putting out the lanterns?
fields.content:
One lantern has gone dark every week since the heroes arrived.

Suspects: the lamplighter (in debt), the miller's daughter (seen near the bog), something from the bog itself.

Deadline: the next new moon - session 5.

fields.title: Party loot ledger
fields.content:
Shared purse: 412 gp, 30 sp.

3 potions of healing (Maelis)
1 potion of water breathing (Kiri)
Silver hand mirror from Castle Verrin (unidentified)
False map of the Thornwood (Fenwick insists it is useful)

Owed to Durgan from the shared purse: 20 gp for the toll bridge.

fields.title: The plan (it did not survive)
fields.content:
Step 1: Brakka gets hired as a vault guard.
Step 2: Captain Marr gets the blueprints.
Step 3: Varric causes a distraction at the pie contest.
Step 4: walk out with the gold during the fireworks.

Update after part two: there was no gold. We have a door.

fields.title: Inspiration and mood board
fields.content:
Mood board: https://files.example.com/sunken-library/moodboard

Think of flooded reading rooms, lantern light on water and index cards that rearrange themselves.

No homework - this is only for those who like to read ahead.

fields.title: What to bring to your first game
fields.content:
Nothing! Dice, pencils and ready-made heroes are waiting at the table.

If you want your own character, create a hero of level 1 on this site and choose it on the campaign page.

We start at noon and finish by four.

fields.title: Seraphine's missing mentor
fields.content:
Maestro Oriel Vance vanished from the Ember Court two years ago. Clues so far:

His song was the arsonist's signal (session 1).
Smugglers' caves: a music box that plays the same melody (session 3).
A rescued sailor wears his ring (session 6).

Next step: get the sailor talking before the Admiral's people do.

fields.title: People of Blackmoor
fields.content:
The lamplighter, Josef - friendly, exhausted, lying about something.
Widow Harrow - sells candles, knows the secrets of every family.
The miller's daughter, Anka - not afraid of the bog, which is suspicious on its own.

Ember trusts Anka. Captain Marr does not trust anyone, so that tells us nothing.
